speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Before I begin, in the context of my Adjournment Motion, I would like to declare that I am a consultant psychiatrist in private practice, I hold a visiting consultant psychiatrist appointment in a restructured hospital and I am the honorary secretary of the Singapore Psychiatric Association.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There is greater awareness of mental health issues, wider efforts at integrating mental health into primary care, a readiness in the use of telehealth and a greater appreciation and initiation of mental health initiatives amongst youths.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There is also greater emphasis on research and local data to help inform policy decisions and allocate resource to areas most in need.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Since July 2021, we have had the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being look into three focus areas: the first of which relates to improving accessibility, coordination and quality of mental health services, the second seeking to strengthen services and support for youth mental well-being, and the third to improve workplace wellbeing measures and employment support.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: My Motion speaks most loudly to the first focus area and how I think we can and must do better in delivering mental healthcare and make it accessible to all.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: A path itself is not enough for it to be called accessible.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Taking a leaf from the transportation industry, to get people and goods from one destination to another, we pave ourselves a myriad and network of walkways, park connectors, roads, tracks and expressways – underground, on the surface and above ground.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We maintain them to a tee to prevent potholes and disrepair.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We want to make the journey smooth for our road users to get to their destinations of choice so that when they reach the destination, they are comfortable and ready for their intended tasks rather than be exhausted from the navigation of the journey itself.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We ensure there is timely intervention and quick removal of barriers for traffic to resume especially during peak hours.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: And we also manage capacity of our transport systems to ensure we are able to sufficiently absorb the demand on a daily basis.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There are clear alternatives routes and diversions as part of the forward planning in the transport infrastructure.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: And to our best efforts, we also ensure that transportation and people movement are safe and compatible with the users of the day.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: First, accessibility means that, at the time of need, there is reasonable expedient mental healthcare and there is capacity in the system to be able to accommodate.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We need to ensure our lanes are wide enough to receive and the roadside lamps are up and the potholes are cleared for passage.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I would be interested to see what our mean numbers are, because there could well be a long tail in terms of the waiting time for patients to get professional help beyond the 50th percentile.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: For psychiatric departments in restructured hospitals, manpower and infrastructure continues to be stretched to address the increasingly complex medico-psychiatric cases, cases involving vulnerable adults and those lacking mental capacity.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Cases where trauma, cancer, strokes, infectious diseases and endocrinological illness overlap with mental illness, there is much complexity in the treatment of psychiatric conditions.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Our restructured hospitals have organic psychiatric departments that are smaller, yet the range and depth of complexity of the cases and the need for interdisciplinary work across specialities are no less challenging.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Not all restructured hospitals have dedicated infrastructure and a ward for psychiatric patients and this makes managing even patients, who are of moderate risk, sometimes difficult in a restructured hospital setting.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We are not saying that every time we need to get to the destination, it must be the expressway all the time, but where that is not possible, fair and ready alternatives should be within reach.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, for patients suffering from mental health conditions, they find themselves also stuck between a rock and a very, very hard place.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: For many of them, to search for alternatives beyond what is available in the public healthcare system remains both a rarity and at steep expense.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In our last September Parliamentary Sitting, the House would recall hon Members Dr Tan Wu Meng and Ms He Ting Ru asking about insurance coverage for individuals with mental health conditions.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, the response from the Ministry, in my humble view, skirts the point.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: While I am grateful that Singaporeans and Permanent Residents are covered under MediShield Life regardless of pre-existing conditions, the tenor and the spirit of the questions were that of stigma and a lack of parity and transparency for patients who have a history of mental illness, in procuring insurance coverage for themselves.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There are challenges that people with mental illness face with insurance coverage that goes beyond the scope of their mental illness or the insurance underwriting on their risk of self-harm.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Some find it disproportionately more challenging to secure insurance coverage even for physical health conditions, even though the specific mental health condition they have, or may have had in the past, does not necessarily bear a correlation to a prospective risk of physical ailment per se.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Sometimes, depression can be the result of a temporary but extraordinary loss of a loved one and the likelihood of recurrence may be no different from anyone here in the House.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Attention-deficient hyperactivity disorder can be outgrown for many, with little reliance of medications into adulthood for some.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Dyslexia can be overcome and strategies learnt to manage reading challenges.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Anorexia can be stabilised, self-esteem restored and meaningful relationships blossom thereafter.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Give each mental illness the proper airing and stratification it deserves.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: If we get it right, more people will be willing to get themselves insured.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: More people will take active steps about declaring their conditions and many more others will start taking care of their mental health by seeking treatment early.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I am not saying that insurance is the silver bullet to mental healthcare, but it signals to people that we take it seriously, that we want to prevent it and that we want to make mental healthcare as accessible as possible, especially to those who take a keen interest in wanting to manage their health needs proactively.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Thirdly, accessibility also means ensuring that we manage the intersections of mental healthcare well.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: My hope is that, in tandem with this increase in capacity, that the Government takes heed to the increasing demand of mental healthcare in the coming years and that alongside this, so too would the resources for mental healthcare improve and increase at both primary and tertiary levels of care.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In wanting to improve accessibility through health and mind clinics, my hope is that all future 32 polyclinics will see mental healthcare as part of their staple baseline services by our family physicians.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The Government should also harness stronger lateral linkages across public, people, private sector partnerships as part of a layered approach to deal with mental well-being, mental illness and mental healthcare.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I also hope for better vertical integration of services such that the delivery of mental healthcare from community to hospital, and then back to community can be seamless and less disjointed.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Efficiency, Mr Speaker, sometimes inadvertently means that the hand-off from one point of care to another becomes narrow but steep because the boundaries can be so well-defined and mutually exclusive.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I urge the Government to consider some overlaps at the intersections of mental healthcare, so that the patient journey is seamless and gaps are prevented by design.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: When care touchpoints become more coherent and less fragmented, the patient will feel that the intersections are less ominous and less overbearing and that their last-mile experience in this journey is one of care and deep concern.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This directly ties to their confidence in the quality and delivery of care, their willingness to continue in the care journey and that should they relapse again, they will have little difficulty in navigating the system to find their way to recovery.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Fourthly, accessibility also means accounting for socio-cultural needs and being sensitive to community-specific factors to mental healthcare.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Not all vehicles are made the same, but every vehicle needs servicing even as they each may be unique in some ways.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It is not uncommon that symptoms of depression, obsessive compulsive disorder and psychotic disorders, much as they are recognised and established mental illnesses, take root, shape and form in the socio-religious and cultural background of a patient.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: If we want to make mental healthcare effective, we must consider, as part of our system of care, a deep understanding and sensitivity to the different mores of cultures, faiths and spirituality too.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: When practice of mental healthcare is devoid of this understanding, a diagnosis could be misinformed, treatment becomes sub-optimal, medication compliance becomes poor and a willingness for treatment is lost.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, it can be a barrier to seeking help altogether.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: (In Malay):   For example, Mr Speaker, within the Muslim community, many see the symptoms of mental illness as a spiritual disorder, instigation of evil spirits and caused by something supernatural.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This is despite the fact that the symptoms and causes of mental illness are clearly displayed.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Just like other communities and ethnic groups, efforts to create awareness about mental illness are sometimes challenging.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It requires close cooperation and partners from the Government, community bodies, religious bodies and social agencies.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There should be a deeper conversation about mental health in society, and it should be on everyone's lips just like physical health matters and other prominent issues.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In dealing with mental health comprehensively, while it is not a requirement when seeking treatment, if there are experts who possess a deep understanding and sensitivity towards cultural issues, it will provide comfort and ease to patients, so that they can express their feelings and share their personal difficulties without fear of being ridiculed or having their faith, piety or masculinity feeling diminished.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, through my own clinical lens, I have been educated by patients on their hallucinatory perception of visitations of the occasional deity and spiritual disturbance, whether by Guan Yin, or an omnipotent God or a memory of a distant figure of the past.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This is common across very many different faiths, culture and backgrounds.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: And often, there is an overlay of mental illness that needs addressing and can be helped, not in isolation but through partnership with community and religious institutions playing a part.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Beyond medical-related factors, we must also recognise the interplay of culture, spirituality, faith, gender roles and familial factors as potentially being enablers or barriers to seeking help.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Other than children and the vulnerable in our midst, men and the elderly, in particular, should also be given some focus as we seek to make delivery of mental healthcare culturally competent and more accessible.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, accessibility begins at home and at the workplace.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The process of seeking help is a non-starter when the home and workplace are apprehensive to or unsupportive of mental healthcare.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It would be difficult for employees to seek help when the opportunity cost of declaring their mental health condition could be their entire employment.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The oft-cited question is that of stigma and how can workplaces and employers engender a better culture of mental well-being.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, I look forward to the details in place and the extent to which people with mental health conditions can feel assured regarding their employment.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Beyond this, we must ask ourselves how we can do better on rehabilitative mental health and improve outcomes for re-employment and re-integration of persons with mental health conditions.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: A negative prospect of returning back to their home and livelihoods will feed into people's fears of seeking help early, thinking that they may never return to full function and that there are few opportunities for meaningful employment after a diagnosis of mental illness.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: To conclude, Mr Speaker, I would like to take the opportunity to remind the House that World Mental Health Day is on 10 October.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I will confess that even as I filed this Adjournment Motion, I had forgotten about this fact and I can only posit that it is serendipitous that a psychiatrist is here, winning a ballot to speak on the issue of accessibility of mental healthcare in Parliament just a week before we celebrate World Mental Health Day.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I ask this House to consider the weight of mental illness on our society and measure its funding, resource and accessibility to care accordingly.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Like diabetes, mental illness is often silent and unseen.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, unlike diabetes, the impact of mental Illness on quality of life is more immediate from the point of diagnosis and the grind and burden on caregivers can be immeasurable and very quickly so.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I look forward to this House taking steps to set the tone and example through the work that we do and engagements that we have to make mental healthcare more accessible for all.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: That is a great maiden speech, Dr Syed Harun.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I am also grateful that Dr Syed Harun has chosen to speak on this important topic in his maiden speech in this House.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Younger adults aged 18 to 29 years old seem more affected with about a quarter of those surveyed reporting having poor mental health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Singapore Youth Epidemiology and Resilience Study findings released earlier this year also showed that one in three youths reported mental health symptoms, such as sadness, anxiety and loneliness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Good mental health is essential in maintaining overall health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A person's mental health and well-being is influenced by many factors, such as pressures at work, school, poor relationships and so on.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Addressing these issues will require a collaborative and integrated approach that involves multiple stakeholders from the health, social, education, workplace and community sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Therefore, beside expanding healthcare capacity and investing in training of our healthcare manpower, we need to go beyond curing mental health conditions to prevention and tackle upstream factors through a holistic and coherent strategy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This move upstream means we can avoid over-medicalising mental health conditions and instead invest our resources in the promotion of well-being and early intervention.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This will help us to improve our overall health outcomes and reduce health inequalities across the population.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For these reasons, the Inter-agency Task Force on Mental Health and Well-being was established in July 2022 to oversee and coordinate mental health efforts across different sectors focusing on cross-cutting issues that require inter-agency collaborations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Task Force is chaired by Senior Minister of State for Health Dr Janil Puthucheary and brings together members from over 30 public, private and people sector agencies, including colleagues from the education, social and workplace domains.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ahead of the release of the strategy report, allow me to provide some responses to the issues raised by Dr Syed Harun.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We fully agree with Dr Syed Harun on the importance of taking an active approach towards ensuring accessibility and timeliness of care, capacity and support structures around mental health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For this reason, we believe in preventing poor mental health upstream by equipping every Singaporean with basic awareness and literacy on mental health and well-being issues and encouraging those in distress to actively seek help when needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Efforts in this space include the Health Promotion Boards (HPB), mysg portal and the "It's okay to reach out" campaign, which promotes self-help and provide guidance on maintaining good mental well-being, such as managing emotions and stress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond literacy and awareness, it is also important to dispel stigma and misconceptions around the topic of mental health and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The National Council of Social Services (NCSS), beyond the Labour Movement, addresses mental health stigma and promotes social inclusion of persons with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We hope that through these efforts we can build better awareness, improve understanding and normalise conversations around mental health of Singaporeans from all ethnic and religious groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond general public education efforts, we have been enhancing community resources to make it easier for Singaporeans to seek help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For instance, well-being circles have been set up to provide citizens the skills to care for their own mental well-being and that of others around them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In addition, community mental health teams supported by the Government and set up by social service agencies provide mental health assessment and psychosocial help for those in distress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Many of these services are provided without charge to their residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Specifically for the Malay/Muslim community, I am leading a new focus area on community Health set up under M3, a collaborative effort between the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore, MENDAKI and madrasahs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The aim is to rally the Malay/Muslim community in promoting healthy living lifestyles and empowering them to organise and scale community-led initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One of its priority areas include supporting the mental health and well-being of the residents, taking into account their cultural context.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will leverage on this effort to bring across more mental well-being initiatives to the residents through further collaborations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We note Dr Syed Harun's concerns on health insurance coverage for individuals with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some individuals may wish to purchase private Integrated Shield Plans and other insurance plans beyond subsidies and MediShield Life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Private insurers selling these plans are expected to deal fairly with customers and not to indiscriminately reject an application solely based on declared personal information, such as occupation, income, disability or medical condition, including mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Lastly, we recognise the importance of workplace and employment support for individuals with mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: On this front, companies are encouraged to tap on the various initiative's available, such as the HPB's Workplace Outreach Wellness package, which supports companies in rolling out general workplace health programmes, including mental health workshops based on their employees' needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mental health is integral to overall health and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There are plans in the pipeline to address mental health issues holistically over the next few years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With the release of the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy Report, we invite the members of public to go through the report, understand the strategy and plans and put up further ideas and suggestions for discussion.
